the cause, measured, and how I fix it

This is the one gap card 51 found, now with pictures instead of a table.

THE PROBLEM. Show completed tasks hides things and never says how many. Every other control in this app that hides something tells you the number — Missed does, and the tree’s tab row reads Completed (1), Past due (1), Deleted (0). So you could have three finished subtasks tucked behind that line and nothing on screen would say so.

THE FIX. The line now carries its number, in the same red as Missed’s, in the same place.

The number cannot drift from the list. It is counted from the same rows and the same test the filter itself uses one line above (if (n.done) hide = !S.done). Counting separately is exactly how the tree’s Completed tab once came to read “(1)” over an empty list — that is written in your own planner as card 3’s comment, and this does not repeat it.

THE WORDING, changed at your word 2026-11-05. Both hiding lines now say tasks, not subtasks:

Show future subtasks  →  Show future tasks
Show completed subtasks  →  Show completed tasks
Six gates named the old wording and would have gone silently stale or started failing on a rename. All six are updated in the same pass, so nothing is left searching for text that no longer exists.

TWO THINGS I FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT, both already in your live planner:
  1. A zero would never have appeared at all. The menu builder said if (opts.count), and 0 is falsy in JavaScript — so a line with nothing behind it would have shown no number, which is the exact ambiguity this card removes. Your tree already prints Deleted (0), so zero is a number this app shows. Fixed.
  2. A dead menu line looked exactly like a live one. I measured the rendered colours: a disabled line and a clickable line were both rgb(233,236,241) at full opacity, because nothing in the file ever styled a disabled gear line. That means Missed has been shipping as a line that looks pressable and silently does nothing. Now a dead line goes grey, and so does its number — a red number means “these are waiting for you”, and zero of them is not.
Missed is untouched. It passes null rather than 0, so it still reads exactly as the tree’s Missed does — dimmed, with no number — now that zeros print.

The picture shows: the gear menu with three completed subtasks hidden behind the line.

And the second case: the same menu with nothing completed at all — the case that proves the number is real and not decoration.
